paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this whole passage is shouting at us. After chapters of Job and his friends trying to figure God out, the LORD doesn't hand Job an explanation. He asks, "Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?" (Job 38:4). The point isn't to embarrass Job. It's that the One asking is the One who made everything, and Job is not the one holding it up.

And look at how carefully He holds it. He shut the sea in behind doors and said, "You may come this far, but no farther" (Job 38:11). He sends rain "on a desert where no man lives" (Job 38:26). Nobody is watching that desert, and it's still on His mind. I think if He's that careful with a patch of wasteland nobody will ever visit, then your hard season is not out of His sight, baker.

So here's what to bake into your heart. You don't have to understand everything to trust the One who does. "Who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind?" (Job 38:36). Every bit of wisdom you have came from Him, so when your questions pile up higher than a flour sack, bring them to Him and let Him be God. And friend, this story is NOT over.
